html:
The global security landscape is dominated by escalating US-Iran conflict in the Middle East, marked by direct military actions and threats, alongside significant uncertainty surrounding a newly signed US-Saudi civilian nuclear cooperation agreement. This volatile situation is further complicated by President Trump’s insistence that the deal is contingent on Saudi Arabia normalizing relations with Israel.

US-Iran Escalation: Iranian and Iran-backed Houthi forces have intensified actions across the Middle East, with Houthis attacking Saudi vessels and claiming a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia, raising fears of wider conflict and global economic damage. Iran also reported stopping three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and launching drone attacks on US bases in Kuwait and Jordan, with reports of American casualties. US forces have conducted multiple strikes on Iran, targeting infrastructure and aiming to "further degrade" military capabilities, while President Trump has warned of a "massive attack" and threatened "major military punishment." The UN Secretary general António Guterres has warned the Middle East crisis is "getting out of control." The US House of Representatives passed a resolution to curb the Trump administration's military action in Iran, though the Senate failed to pass a related War Powers resolution.

US-Saudi Nuclear Deal: A new US-Saudi civilian nuclear cooperation agreement, expected to last decades and be worth billions, has been thrown into turmoil by President Trump’s declaration that it is "totally subject to" Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords and recognizing Israel. This condition, revealed online by Trump the day after the deal was signed, contradicts Riyadh's long-standing resistance to normalization without a pathway to a Palestinian state, and has reportedly raised alarm in Israel and other US allies.

Global Economy & Markets: Global markets are reacting to multiple pressures, with Google and Tesla shares plunging as investors question the financial benefits of extensive AI spending. The escalating Middle East conflict has driven oil prices higher, with the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea crises pushing prices to $96. The European Central Bank has kept interest rates unchanged, noting it is "closely monitoring" the energy price shock and its impact on inflation. In other economic news, about 200 firms have signed President Trump’s non-binding "Ratepayer Protection Pledge" aiming to protect US consumers from the costs of AI datacenter build-out.

Ukraine & Great Power Dynamics: In Ukraine, ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov continues to refuse President Zelensky’s offer of an alternative post, insisting on reinstatement amidst a political crisis. Meanwhile, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov held a face-to-face meeting on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila, marking their first talks in over a year, as Washington seeks to revive mediation efforts to end the war. Elsewhere, Sweden has eased mining permits for critical minerals, declaring it a national security interest to reduce dependence on China. China, in turn, is reportedly rewriting its "Soft Power" playbook for the AI age, with Xi pursuing AI diplomacy to "woo global south."

Major Global Events: Diverse global events include Sonam Wangchuk, an India activist, ending a 26-day hunger strike, following protests demanding education reforms that have grown into one of India’s largest anti-government movements. France is evacuating 20,000 people, mostly tourists, as wildfires spread rapidly in the south-west Gironde region. The Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 1,000, marking the fastest fatal surge on record. Concerns are also growing in Southern California over a cluster of "exceptionally rare" cancer cases in the Ladera Ranch community.
